new_statements.relation_note: Handwritten key of Luce's five 'basic tones' with the dialects that have each: Ngɔn is entered under 1 High (or Mid) Level, 3 Rising and 4 Low Falling, and is absent from 2 High Falling and 5 Low Level, i.e. a three-tone system (tones 1, 3, 4) -- the manuscript basis of the typescript 'Table H. Basic tones in Chin' already held (NGƆːN ha¹ 'teeth', nga³ 'fish', za⁴ 'hundred'). The preceding sheets give each etymon's Ngawn tone number under tone-pattern Types I (Ngawn 4), II (Ngawn 1), III (Ngawn 3) for three village varieties. No prose, nothing on stress, syllable weight or prominence.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ngawn (Ngɔn) has three lexical tones in Luce's 1954-55 analysis: high/mid level (his tone 1), rising (tone 3) and low falling (tone 4); no falling-vs-low-level contrast as in Sizang/Zanniat/Haka.
new_statements.identity_note: Columns headed 'Ngɔːn I, II, III' (p. 043) and 'Ngɔn (Zolpi)', 'Ngɔn (Bwalkaw)', 'Ngɔn (Hɔːzɔŋ)' (pp. 044-047) = Luce's three Ngawn (Ngorn) informants' villages Zawlpi, Bualkhua, Hauzang(?) in Falam township, the same three Ngɔːn columns as in the held folder-22/29 tables; p. 051 header lists 'Zawlpi Hɔzang Bwalkhaw / Lumbang Lan-tawn' and 'Stephen Khup Tin Pau 5 p.m.'.
